bonuses.requirements: Banking Sector Reportedly Pauses Bond Issuance for Texas Data Center Related to AnthropicHomeFeedNewsBanking Sector Reportedly Pauses Bond Issuance for Texas Data Center Related to AnthropicBanking Sector Reportedly Pauses Bond Issuance for Texas Data Center Related to Anthropic10/28 23:11On October 29, it was reported that banks are delaying the sale of a $15 billion loan intended to fund bond issuance for data centers related to Anthropic PBC, following the suspension of new project approvals in Texas due to assessments of grid risks. This postponement occurs as Anthropic is heavily investing in computing infrastructure ahead of its large-scale initial public offering (IPO), which will force banks to hold this debt on their balance sheets longer than originally planned. Led by Morgan Stanley, lenders have raised approximately $15 billion to finance the construction of data centers located near Hubbard, Texas. According to informed sources, banks had initially hoped to sell $5 billion to $7 billion to high-yield bond investors in September to refinance part of the loan. Now, the sales may occur in batches over the next year. Popular Cardano stake pool operator Sssebi has highlighted a major development on $ADA’s weekly chart, noting that the token has finally broken above a key multi-year resistance level.

In a post on X, Sssebi pointed to Cardano’s weekly close above a resistance zone that had constrained $ADA price for years. Based on his accompanying chart, the key level sits around $0.24, which previously served as a major barrier during $ADA’s prolonged downtrend and consolidation.

$ADA ultimately closed the week above that level, with the chart showing the token reaching $0.248. This weekly close is notable because it shows that buyers managed to push $ADA through a price area that had previously rejected attempts to move higher.

He attributed the correction largely to capital shifting from cryptocurrencies into AI-related equities, leaving the crypto market short of free funds as AI investments appear more attractive. However, he believes this could change as financial conditions improve.

Pal predicts the crypto market capitalization could reach $10 trillion within a few years and $100 trillion by 2035 — a 40x increase from the current $2.5 trillion valuation.

He also sees AI agents — programs capable of autonomously performing tasks and making payments — as a key driver of future crypto demand. He estimates their number could reach 25 billion by 2027, and if even 1% adopt crypto wallets, that would mean 250 million new participants in the digital economy.#$100 Trillion#AI Agents#AI Competition#Crypto Market#Crypto Wallets#Digital Economy#Market Cap Forecast#Market Correction#Raoul Pal#SupercycleThe correction that has now begun does not mean the end of the bull cycle, the entrepreneur and investor said, speaking at the TOKEN2049 conference. He named the shift of part of investors' capital from cryptocurrencies into shares of companies involved in artificial intelligence (AI) as an important cause of the correction. The crypto market has faced a shortage of available funds, since investments in AI look more attractive. However, according to Pal, the situation may change—as financial conditions improve.

GENIUS Act Detailed Rules Take Effect, Crypto Market Welcomes These Benefits | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsProject UpdatesGENIUS Act Detailed Rules Take...GENIUS Act Detailed Rules Take Effect, Crypto Market Welcomes These BenefitsOdaily星球日报Published on 2026-10-22Last updated on 2026-10-22AbstractThe OCC has released final rules implementing the GENIUS Act, marking a key step in U.S. stablecoin regulation. The rules, effective January 18, 2027, clarify requirements for payment stablecoin issuance, reserves, redemption, custody, and risk management. Stablecoin issuers must hold sufficient qualifying reserves—such as cash, eligible bank deposits, and short-term U.S. Treasuries—and establish clear redemption policies. Banks may issue through compliant subsidiaries, while non-bank firms can seek federal qualification.

A notable change from the draft removes the presumption that certain third-party reward arrangements violate the ban on paying interest. Rewards distributed by exchanges or partners will now be reviewed case by case, preserving some room for platforms to attract users, though the issuer interest ban remains. Another change cancels automatic redemption extensions when large redemption requests exceed 10% of outstanding issuance within 24 hours.

The banking industry, especially community banks, opposes these looser reward rules, warning they could draw deposits away from banks and reduce community bank lending. Beneficiaries may include stablecoin issuers like Circle and Coinbase, payment infrastructure providers, DeFi and RWA platforms, and public blockchains hosting stablecoin activity. Broader stablecoin adoption could also bring new fiat inflows into crypto, potentially creating fresh demand for BTC and ETH.#GENIUS Price#GENIUS Regular Invest#GENIUS Surge#GENIUS Plunge#Bank Opposition#Crypto Market Benefits#DeFi and RWA#GENIUS Act#Interest Payment Ban#OCC Final Rules#On-Chain Dollar Inflow#Redemption Policy#Reserve Requirements#Stablecoin Rules#Third-Pa

bonuses.requirements: FuriosaAI Secures $620 Million in Funding, Valuation Reaches $2.9 BillionHomeFeedNewsFuriosaAI Secures $620 Million in Funding, Valuation Reaches $2.9 BillionFuriosaAI Secures $620 Million in Funding, Valuation Reaches $2.9 Billion10/28 23:30According to Bloomberg, South Korean AI chip startup FuriosaAI has announced the completion of a $620 million Series D funding round, raising its valuation to $2.9 billion, approximately four times its previous valuation of $735 million. Investors include the U.S. firm Infinitum Partners, the Korean National Growth Fund (which contributed $280 million), Jericho Capital, Worldline Capital, Singapore's QUDA Capital, and Abu Dhabi's NeoFort Holding. Existing shareholders such as Naver, Korea Development Bank, DSC Investment, Nextrans, and Kakao Investment also participated, with the Korea Export-Import Bank making its first direct investment in a startup. Founded in 2017, FuriosaAI began mass production of its RNGD inference chips in January this year and is collaborating with Broadcom to develop a third-generation accelerator.
